correctness.rationale: On every bounded complete support trajectory, variation of constants gives y(t)=integral_{-infinity}^t exp(-(t-u))x(u)^2 du. Equality y=0 would force x=0 on an entire backward half-orbit and then zdot=1 there, contradicting bounded completeness, so y>0. Generator invariance with arbitrary antiderivative test functions of x gives E[yz|x]=-a. The same argument in z and y yields E[x|z]=1/4 and E[x^2|y]=y, hence Ex=1/4 and Ey=1/16+Var(x). Since D=E[(1-4x)^2]=16 Var(x), Ey=(1+D)/16 and y-weighting gives E_nu[z]=-16a/(1+D). If D=0 then x=1/4 on the support; bounded completeness of ydot=1/16-y forces y=1/16 and tangency of xdot forces z=-16a, so the measure is the equilibrium Dirac mass. The strict excursion conclusions then follow from equivalence of mu and the positive y-weighted measure. The exact verifier independently checks the polynomial and moment algebra.

final_claim: For the Wang--Chen flow xdot=yz+a, ydot=x^2-y, zdot=1-4x with a>0, every compactly supported invariant probability measure has y>0 on its support, E[yz|x]=-a, and under y-weighting satisfies E_nu[z]=-16a/(1+D), D=E[(1-4x)^2]; D=0 exactly for the equilibrium Dirac mass, so every non-equilibrium compact stationary state has weighted mean strictly between -16a and 0 and positive mass both above the equilibrium height and below zero.
scientific_limitations: The complete 2020 global-geometry article was not materially available in full text; a hidden stationary identity there remains a specific priority risk.
Related stationary-balance results for neighboring Sprott/Chen systems are abundant and may contain an equivalent method, though no same-system implication was found.
The theorem assumes compact support and does not prove existence or basin structure of the non-point attractors.
The y-weighted measure is a diagnostic reweighting and is not claimed to be invariant.
